messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testOverrideVarianceWithMathClass` sets a custom variance implementation of type `Variance` (population variance, as indicated by `new Variance(false)`) into a `SummaryStatistics` object using `setVarianceImpl`. The test then adds data points and expects the variance from the custom `Variance` instance to match the variance computed by `SummaryStatistics`.

The issue arises as the current bug report states: when `SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl(new Variance(true/false))` is called, `getStandardDeviation()` produces NaN.

Examining the relevant code snippets:

- `SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl` calls `checkEmpty()`. The check enforces that no values have been added yet (`n > 0` causes an exception), ensuring the variance implementation can only be replaced when empty.
- `getVariance()` returns `varianceImpl.getResult()`.
- `Variance.getResult()` returns NaN if no data points exist (`moment.n == 0`), returns 0 if only one data point, and computes variance otherwise.
- `Variance` uses `SecondMoment` to accumulate stats. `SecondMoment` initializes its second moment field (`m2`) as NaN.
- `getStandardDeviation()` in `SummaryStatistics` returns NaN if no data or insufficient data; otherwise, it returns the square root of the variance.

The problem likely arises because when `Variance` is set via `setVarianceImpl`, it has no internal data state. Adding values to `SummaryStatistics` may not propagate correctly to `varianceImpl` since it is replaced after the original data handling is bypassed. The internal moment data (`SecondMoment`) in `Variance` remains uninitialized or NaN, causing `getResult()` to return NaN, propagating through to `getVariance()` and `getStandardDeviation()`.

The test seems to expect that adding values to `SummaryStatistics` will update the `Variance` instance's internal data (via `moment`), but this is not happening due to the way `SummaryStatistics` handles delegation to `varianceImpl` (likely it does not forward calls or state updates correctly after `setVarianceImpl`).

Hence, `getStandardDeviation()` computes the square root of NaN variance, resulting in NaN, failing the test which expects the population variance to be computed correctly.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this variance/statistics issue.

Summary:
- Setting a new variance implementation does not properly propagate added values, causing the internal state in `Variance` to remain NaN.
- Consequently, `getVariance()` and `getStandardDeviation()` return NaN.
- The test expects proper propagation and computation of population variance and standard deviation, but the current design or implementation fails to do so.

This explains why the test fails and the standard deviation returns NaN after setting a new variance implementation in `SummaryStatistics`.

Next, methods that should be reviewed include `SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl`, `SummaryStatistics.addValue`, and possibly how `Variance.getResult()` and state update happens.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
